transcript.text: My fridge freezer has been making a funny smell in the kitchen the last couple of days, I've cleaned it out but it's still there. Any ideas?

A 'funny smell' can range from simple organic decay to something more serious like overheating electrical components. First, please check if the smell has any distinct character: is it a sour/rotten food smell, or does it smell like burning plastic/electrical? This distinction is vital for safety. Second, I need the make and model number of your fridge-freezer. This is usually found on a sticker inside the compartment (often near the salad drawer) or on the frame around the door opening. Could you read that out to me?
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]

It smells like hot plastic, a sort of electrical burning smell, not rotten food. It's stronger round the back and side of the fridge than inside it. The model on the label inside is CDA543FS, made by Beko.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. Please switch the fridge-freezer off at the wall and unplug it immediately. A burning plastic or electrical smell, especially coming from the back or side where the mains cable and compressor components are located, is a serious safety warning indicating an overheating wire, faulty plug, or failing electrical component like the start relay. Do not try to use the appliance again until a qualified engineer has inspected it. Continuing to run it could cause a fire or damage other parts. Please contact a repair service or Beko support for a safe diagnosis.

The fault they reported is: "funny smell in the kitchen". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Say what that suggests, then ask for the make and model number so we can find the right part; say it is usually on a sticker inside the fridge, usually on a side wall near the salad drawer. If the label cannot be reached right now (for example the door will not open), say it can wait.
